question.worked_solution:
First, we calculate the derivative using the product rule and sum rule:

$$
\begin{aligned}{g}^{′}(x) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}\,(-4{e}^{x}\operatorname{csc}⁡x+6) \\  & =\frac{d}{dx}(-4{e}^{x})\cdot \operatorname{csc}⁡x+(-4{e}^{x})\cdot \frac{d}{dx}(\operatorname{csc}⁡x)+\frac{d}{dx}(6) \\  & =-4{e}^{x}\operatorname{csc}⁡x+(-4{e}^{x})(-\operatorname{csc}⁡x\operatorname{cot}⁡x)+0 \\  & =-4{e}^{x}\operatorname{csc}⁡x+4{e}^{x}\operatorname{csc}⁡x\operatorname{cot}⁡x \\  & =-4{e}^{x}\operatorname{csc}⁡x(1-\operatorname{cot}⁡x)\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we substitute $x=\frac{\pi }{2}$ and evaluate the slope $m:$

$$
\begin{aligned}m={g}^{′}(\frac{\pi }{2}) & =-4{e}^{\pi /2}\operatorname{csc}⁡(\frac{\pi }{2})(1-\operatorname{cot}⁡(\frac{\pi }{2})) \\  & =-4{e}^{\pi /2}\end{aligned}
$$
